cards.explanation: The answer is that He withdraws to Galilee. Matthew says, “…He withdrew to Galilee.” (Matthew 4:12) John, the man who baptized Jesus (Matthew 3:13), has been put in prison, and Jesus heads for Galilee. The text doesn't tell us why, friends, so I won't make something up. I'll just say it's a quiet move, and the big stuff starts right after.

The answer is Capernaum. Matthew says Jesus went and lived there, by the sea in the region of Zebulun and Naphtali. Notice that He doesn't just pass through. He moves in. A fresh town, a fresh start, nothing like the junk drawer I got shoved into for years.

The answer is light. Isaiah, the prophet, said, “…the people living in darkness have seen a great light…” (Matthew 4:16) Matthew says Jesus moving to Capernaum fulfills those words (Matthew 4:13-14). I know a little about living in the dark, friends, and when the light finally showed up in my life, I felt it.

The answer is that they leave their nets at once. Matthew says, “And at once they left their nets and followed Him.” Simon Peter and Andrew are fishermen, and those nets are their work. When the angel called me out of that junk drawer, I asked for one minute first. Matthew's word for these two is at once.

The answer is their father Zebedee. Matthew says James and his brother John “…were in a boat with their father Zebedee, mending their nets.” Three of them, one boat, and nets to mend. The text puts them all together right there.

The answer is True. Matthew says, “…immediately they left the boat and their father and followed Him.” They didn't wait around. Their father Zebedee was right there in the boat with them, and they still went. Matthew doesn't tell us what Zebedee said, friends, so I won't invent a line for him.

The answer is in their synagogues. Matthew says Jesus went throughout Galilee, “…teaching in their synagogues…” A synagogue is a place where people gathered, and Jesus taught in them across the whole region. He wasn't staying put in one spot.

The answer is healing every disease and sickness. Matthew says Jesus was “…healing every disease and sickness among the people.” Every one. He's teaching, preaching and healing, all in the same trip through Galilee. That's a lot of ground to cover, friends, and I'm tired just reading it.

The answer is False. Matthew says the large crowds followed Him “…from Galilee, the Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea, and beyond the Jordan.” Galilee is just the start of that list. Those crowds came from all over. I've had my cookie boxes drawing a crowd before, friends, but never like that.
